source_name: Стопанска комора на Северна Македонија (Economic Chamber of North Macedonia)
why_relevant: Oldest and largest business chamber; umbrella for sectoral associations (здруженија), publishes news, regulatory commentary (пропис-инфо), annual activity reports and training programmes including payment-operations (платен промет) trainings. Bilingual mk/en.

source_name: Стопанска комора — Здружение на финансиски организации (Association of Financial Organisations)
why_relevant: The chamber's sectoral association covering banks, insurers, pension fund managers, non-bank financial companies, leasing firms and savings houses in one body — broader than MBA (which is deposit-takers only). Publishes elected leadership (e.g. presidency drawn from Triglav Osiguruvanje and Tigo Finance), meeting conclusions and sector positions.

source_name: Стопанска комора — annual activity reports (Годишен извештај, PDF archive)
why_relevant: Chamber annual reports document which sectoral associations met, what positions were adopted and which companies participated — a durable historical record of banking/payments advocacy. The /Upload/Documents/ path is a predictable PDF repository worth enumerating.

source_name: MASIT — Стопанска комора за информатички и комуникациски технологии
why_relevant: The ICT chamber. Its member pages enumerate the technology suppliers that serve banks and payment companies in MK (e.g. ASEE Group, Endava, Interworks, GDi, Insight Group, Finelevate, plus consultancies like EY). This is the single densest local pointer to the bank-technology vendor layer, which A1 disclosure sources rarely name.

source_name: MASIT legacy site (oldmasit.masit.org.mk) — historical member list
why_relevant: Archived earlier generation of the MASIT member directory. Comparing old vs current membership reveals vendor entries/exits, renames and acquisitions in the MK ICT-to-banking supplier base over time.

source_name: Foreign Investors Council (FIC) North Macedonia — White Book & members
why_relevant: 130+ members from 20 countries explicitly including banking and insurance. The annual White Book is a structured position paper naming regulatory pain points sector by sector — one of the few local documents where foreign-owned banks state policy positions on the record. Also publishes a Business Catalogue (member directory) and press releases.

source_name: AmCham North Macedonia — members and position papers
why_relevant: 140+ member companies including several banks (Komercijalna Banka, Stopanska Banka, ProCredit, NLB) per third-party listings. AmCham issues policy positions, committee outputs and event materials; its member directory is a cross-check on which banks are outward-facing on policy.

source_name: German-Macedonian Business Association (DMWV/МГСЗ) — member directory PDF
why_relevant: 200+ members; the largest bilateral business association in MK and strategic partner of AHK Nordmazedonien. The annually issued Mitgliederverzeichnis is a downloadable, machine-parsable member directory — an unusually clean pointer artefact. Trilingual context (de/mk/en).

source_name: AFD — Alternative Financial Services Association of North Macedonia (Асоцијација за алтернативни финансиски услуги)
why_relevant: Association uniting FinTech companies and non-bank financial service providers operating outside the banking sector in North Macedonia — the counterpart body to MBA for the fintech/consumer-lending segment. Its members and code-of-practice documents are the main pointer to licensed non-bank lenders and payment-adjacent fintechs.

source_name: ACI Macedonia — Financial Markets Association
why_relevant: National chapter of ACI Financial Markets Association: the professional body for bank treasury/FX/money-market dealers. Membership and event materials identify treasury-side practitioners and market conventions, complementing MBA's institution-level view with a practitioner-level one.

source_name: Сојуз на стопански комори на Македонија (Macedonian Chambers of Commerce, MCC)
why_relevant: Second major chamber system (independent of mchamber.mk), described as connecting thousands of member companies to 1000+ national/regional institutions; signs bilateral memoranda (e.g. with the Croatian Chamber) and runs sectoral groupings. A parallel member universe worth diffing against Стопанска комора.

source_name: Стопанска комора на северо-западна Македонија / Oda Ekonomike e Maqedonisë Veriperëndimore (OEMVP)
why_relevant: Regional/ethnic-Albanian business chamber (est. 2005, Skopje), publishing in Albanian and Macedonian. Covers a member base — including Albanian-owned SMEs banking with specific institutions — that the Skopje-centric chambers under-represent. Adds the sq language dimension to the MK association landscape.

source_name: MBA LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Often carries association announcements, event photos and staff/committee signals earlier or more granularly than the website, and surfaces which member-bank executives engage publicly. Useful as an early-warning channel for MBA activity.

source_name: zk.mk business registry entry — МБА Македонска Банкарска Асоцијација
why_relevant: Third-party company-registry aggregator carrying registration identifiers, address and officers for the association itself (and, via the same site, for chambers such as Стопанска комора на северо-западна Македонија). Useful for entity resolution when linking association entities to Central Register filings.

source_name: bankarstvo.mk — Macedonian banking trade portal
why_relevant: Specialist local trade publication covering banking and payment cards (dedicated платежни картички category), including e-commerce and cross-border online-payment trends. Frequently reports association and member-bank announcements that never reach English-language media, and is a discovery channel for association events.

source_name: biznisregulativa.mk — chamber registry profile (МАСИТ and other комори)
why_relevant: Government-adjacent business-regulation portal that enumerates recognised chambers (комори) with profile pages. A compact way to obtain the authoritative list of chamber-type bodies in MK rather than assembling it ad hoc from search results.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of the Republic of North Macedonia (Министерство за финансии) — main portal
why_relevant: Owner of payment-services legislation (Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи), fiscalisation policy, financial-sector strategy and budget. Publishes press releases, draft laws, strategies and sector policy in mk and en (mk-MK / en-GB URL variants).

source_name: Ministry of Finance — archive site (arhiva.finance.gov.mk)
why_relevant: Holds pre-redesign MoF content: older strategies, past press releases and unit pages (e.g. Financial Intelligence Office page, public debt strategies 2022-2026) that were dropped or re-pathed on the new portal. Essential for time-series and for resolving dead links.

source_name: Ministry of Finance — Public Debt Reports / Public Debt Management Strategy
why_relevant: Quarterly/annual public-debt reports and multi-year debt management strategies (current cycle 2025-2027 with 2029 outlook). Indirectly reveals sovereign issuance, bank exposure to government paper and treasury-market plumbing that banks and payment providers depend on.

source_name: Public Revenue Office (Управа за јавни приходи, УЈП) — main portal
why_relevant: Operator of fiscalisation (cash registers) and of the new mandatory e-Invoicing (е-Фактура) regime. Publishes announcements, technical specifications, regulation overviews and enforcement statistics — the single most directly commercially relevant state source for POS/fiscal-device and e-invoicing vendors.

source_name: UJP e-Faktura (е-Фактура) programme documents
why_relevant: Directory of official e-invoicing presentations, XML/UBL standard specs and API integration guidance for the mandate reported as taking effect 1 October 2026. Directly determines ERP/POS vendor product roadmaps in MK.

source_name: State Statistical Office (Државен завод за статистика, ДЗС) — publications
why_relevant: Official releases (соопштенија) and publications by subject area, including monetary/financial and business-sector statistics, ICT usage by households and enterprises (a proxy for digital-payments adoption) and structural business statistics covering financial-services activity.

source_name: MakStat database (PX-Web) — State Statistical Office
why_relevant: Machine-readable time series across all ДЗС domains, exportable as PX/Excel/CSV/JSON with a documented PX-Web API — the cheapest structured feed for MK macro and sector indicators feeding banking/payments analysis.

source_name: State Statistical Office — new domain stat.mk
why_relevant: ДЗС appears to run a second/newer domain (stat.mk) alongside stat.gov.mk, carrying 'За нас', annual reports and institutional documents. Needed so a collector does not miss content published on only one of the two hosts.

source_name: Deposit Insurance Fund (Фонд за осигурување на депозити, ФОД/ФОДСК)
why_relevant: Statutory deposit guarantee scheme for MK banks and savings houses. Publishes annual financial reports, announcements, the legal framework and freedom-of-information disclosures; its payout announcements are the primary signal on failing savings houses/banks.

source_name: Financial Intelligence Office (Управа за финансиско разузнавање, УФР / FIU) — annual reports
why_relevant: The MK FIU sits within the MoF and publishes yearly reports with counts and typologies of suspicious transaction reports by reporting entity type (banks, exchange offices, money remitters, payment institutions) — a rare public window on payments-channel risk and on which institution types are active.

source_name: State Audit Office (Државен завод за ревизија, ДЗР) — audit reports register
why_relevant: Supreme audit institution. Its audit reports on state-linked financial entities, the MoF, UJP, ДЗС and public funds routinely disclose IT-system weaknesses, procurement of fiscal/payment systems, and financial-control failings that no other public source reports.
